The left port is labeled v(t), with the upper end positive and the lower end negative; current i(t) flows from the upper left end to the right along the upper branch. The upper branch is, in order, a 1 Ω resistor and a 1 H inductor, the right vertical branch is a 1 F capacitor, and the bottom wire returns to the negative terminal of the voltage source. Therefore this is a voltage-driven series RLC loop, and the current enters the passive terminal of each element in the direction shown. Reasoning: According to the problem statement, i_L(0-) = 1 A, v_C(0-) = -1 V, and the input v(t)=u(t), so V(s)=1/s. Use the unilateral Laplace transform and write KVL: V(s)=R I(s)+L[sI(s)-i_L(0-)]+V_C(s). The capacitor relation is V_C(s)=[I(s)/C+v_C(0-)]/s. Substituting R=L=C=1, i_L(0-)=1, and v_C(0-)=-1 gives V_C(s)=(I(s)-1)/s. Thus 1/s = I(s) + [sI(s)-1] + [I(s)-1]/s. Multiplying both sides by s: 1 = sI(s)+s^2 I(s)-s+I(s)-1 = (s^2+s+1)I(s)-s-1. Therefore (s^2+s+1)I(s)=s+2, obtaining I(s)=(s+2)/(s^2+s+1).
